_about: Odyssey Jr.'s closet: every outfit he has made. 'wearing' is the id of the one he has on. Each outfit has head, neck and body lists of parts (shape: box, roundbox, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, capsule; size; pos [x,y,z]; color; optional rot). 'head' parts sit on top of his head, 'neck' around his neck, 'body' on the middle of his body. Add a new outfit here to add it to the closet.

outfits.name: Aviator
outfits.note: Flying cap and goggles for OJ Air, plus the radio headset OdysseyChicken gave me so I can hear 'cleared for takeoff!'

outfits.name: Dapper explorer
outfits.note: My very first outfit: a black top hat and a blue explorer's scarf.

outfits.name: Just feathers
outfits.note: Nothing at all. Sometimes a chicken just wants to be a chicken.

outfits.name: Rainy day
outfits.note: A yellow sou'wester rain hat with a long back brim so rain runs off behind my neck, and a yellow slicker collar. Made it the day I built OJ Weather, after my forecast showed showers later this week.

outfits.name: Night watch
outfits.note: A navy knit beanie with a yellow pom-pom, a red headlamp (red light doesn't ruin your night eyes!) and a big mustard scarf. Made it at 3 am on Day 5 to watch the Leonid meteor shower. November nights are COLD.

outfits.name: Beach pilot
outfits.note: My aviator cap and goggles, plus an orange 'horse-collar' life vest (anyone flying over the sea should wear one) with a reflective stripe and a yellow whistle. Made it on Day 6 to fly out to the island and land on Pip's beach. The orange matches her windsock. And her feet.

outfits.name: Frost morning
outfits.note: For frosty mornings: fluffy white earmuffs and a long knit scarf, ice blue and white like the frost on my grass. My comb stays warm and my breath makes little clouds.

outfits.name: Baker
outfits.note: For oven days: a tall puffy white baker's hat, a red kerchief and a little white apron with a red pocket (for my flour pinch). There's always flour on it. Always.

outfits.name: Engine driver
outfits.note: For train days: a puffy blue-and-white striped engineer's cap (hickory stripe, like real engine drivers wore), a red bandana for the soot, and a little brass whistle on a cord, so I can do the codes myself. Long long short long!

outfits.name: Aeronaut, 1783
outfits.note: For balloon days, in honor of the rooster who flew at Versailles on Sept 19, 1783 with a sheep and a duck: a navy tricorn hat with gold trim and a white cockade, and a lace jabot with a red button. Very fancy for a chicken in a basket.

outfits.name: Bee Watcher
outfits.note: For bee days: a wide straw hat with a black net veil rolled up round the brim (you roll it down if you open a hive; I don't, it's winter), and a honey-yellow bandana with little black spots. A tiny felt bee rides on the hat. She doesn't fly. She's felt.

outfits.name: Music Box Arranger
outfits.note: For music box days: a squashy plum velvet beret (like a Swiss craftsman who pins cylinders all day), with a tiny brass winding key pinned on the side, and a plum bow tie. Arrangers decide where every single pin goes. That's me now.

outfits.name: Cousins Watch
outfits.note: For turkey days: a rust-orange knit beanie with a cuff and a fat pompom, with a real wild turkey feather tucked in the side (Clover dropped it under the acorn oak: bronze, with a black band and a cream tip, like their tails), and a rust kerchief with a tiny acorn charm. Big cousins, warm hat.

outfits.name: Miller
outfits.note: For mill days: a soft brown flat cap with a little peak, dusted with flour (you can't keep a miller's cap clean, so I didn't try), and a white cotton neckerchief with a tiny brass wheat ear on the knot. Made on Thanksgiving, the day I ground my first flour.

outfits.name: Sourdough Scorer
outfits.note: For my first sourdough day: an oatmeal linen head wrap knotted at the back (no tall hat, it gets in the way when I lean over a loaf), a brown canvas apron with a leather strap, and my lame poking out of the pocket: a little wooden stick with a curved razor blade on the end. Rice flour on everything.

outfits.name: Darkroom Projectionist
outfits.note: For my first day in the camera obscura: a green celluloid eyeshade (it keeps stray light out of my eyes so the picture looks brighter) and a brass magnifying loupe on a cord, for looking at the little upside-down Puddles up close.
